literal: Arguments not equal to splitting an autumn down — how can they untie the linked rings?
idiomatic: If the reasoning cannot match the finest hair-splitting, how can it loosen the linked rings?

literal: Originally I meant to keep this within my own gate, to leave it for children in their first studies, and also to assist my own foolishness close at hand, privately to fill gaps in memory.
idiomatic: I had meant to keep this within my own household, to leave it for children at their first lessons, and also to shore up my own dullness nearby, privately filling gaps in what I remembered.

literal: I did not realize that on Mount Guye the spirit gathers, that Fenyang streams its radiance — the high listens to the low, and words spoken near at hand are to be examined.
idiomatic: I did not grasp that on Mount Guye the spirit gathers, that Fenyang sends down its light — the lofty hears the humble, and what is said close at hand must be scrutinized.

literal: Late in spring I received the edict and was humbly favored with encouragement; the present sovereign's commentary on the Laozi — I respectfully dare to present it sealed, with a preface as a separate document.
idiomatic: Late in spring I received the edict and was graciously encouraged; the present sovereign's commentary on the Laozi — I respectfully present it sealed, with a preface submitted separately.

literal: " The edict replied: "Master Li roams the spirit in dark obscurity, alone contemplates the dim and vague, is mysteriously one with creation, and takes the multitude of beings as his end.
idiomatic: " The edict replied: "Master Li roams the spirit in the dark void, alone contemplates the dim and vague, is mysteriously one with creation, and takes the multitude of beings as his end.

literal: From within reaching the outer, a comprehensive response can trim and form;
idiomatic: From within reaching outward, a comprehensive response can shape and complete;

literal: from the self to things, operation can supply use.
idiomatic: from the self to things, operation can supply what is needed.

literal: Elevating the family and pacifying the state — the meaning belongs to this learning.
idiomatic: To exalt the house and settle the realm — that meaning belongs to this learning.

literal: Your talent and thought are excellent and thorough; your pursuits are lofty and far-reaching. You rested in the Confucian gate and galloped in the Daoist market — you have both opened specialized learning and expounded the teachings of Buddhism and Laozi.
idiomatic: Your talent and thought are excellent and thorough; your pursuits are lofty and far-reaching. You rested in the Confucian gate and ranged through the Daoist hall — you have both opened a school of your own and made plain the teachings of Buddhism and Laozi.

literal: Households arrayed, gates open; paths connected, routes direct — principle and affairs both expressed, ability and use both displayed. What those worthies had not awakened to, what old recluses had not heard — the aim is utmost subtlety, the words exhaust depth and wonder.
idiomatic: Households arrayed, gates open; paths connected, routes direct — principle and affairs both set forth, ability and use both shown. What those worthies had not grasped, what old recluses had not heard — the aim is utmost subtlety, the words exhaust depth and wonder.

literal: We have taste for the two classics and are weary of old explanations; having reviewed new commentaries, our gain is already great — the esteem we feel comes from more than one source.
idiomatic: We relish the two classics and are weary of old explanations; having reviewed new commentaries, our gain is already great — the esteem we feel does not spring from one cause alone.

literal: We have already ordered it bound in green silk and stored in the Yan Pavilion.
idiomatic: We have already ordered it bound in green silk and stored in the Yan Pavilion.

literal: " He also presented one copy to Gao Huan and one to Shizong.
idiomatic: " He also presented one copy to Gao Huan and one to Shizong.

literal: In the Wuding era he was promoted to Commandant of the Guards.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was promoted to commandant of the guards.

literal: When Liang sent the Marquis of Zhenyang, Xiao Ming, and others to invade Pengcheng, Grand Commander Gao Yue and the expeditionary force Murong Shaozong led the armies to attack them; an edict made Bi army adjutant and acting left director of the expeditionary secretariat.
idiomatic: When Liang sent the Marquis of Zhenyang, Xiao Ming, and others to invade Pengcheng, Grand Commander Gao Yue and expeditionary commander Murong Shaozong led the armies against them; an edict appointed Bi army adjutant and acting left director of the expeditionary secretariat.

literal: Before departure Shizong gave him a Hu horse and said to Bi: "This is the second horse in the stable; I always ride it myself. Now that we part far apart, I offer it to you in passing.
idiomatic: Before he set out, Shizong gave him a Hu horse and said to Bi, "This is the second horse in the stable; I always ride it myself. Now that we part for a distant campaign, I offer it to you in passing.

literal: " He also ordered him to record one or two points of important administration that could serve as mirrors and warnings.
idiomatic: " He also ordered him to set down one or two points of important administration that could serve as mirrors and warnings.

literal: Bi asked to state them orally: "Under Heaven's great tasks, nothing surpasses reward and punishment; reward one man and all under Heaven rejoice, punish one man and all under Heaven submit.
idiomatic: Bi asked to state them orally: "Under Heaven's great tasks, nothing surpasses reward and punishment; reward one man and all under Heaven rejoice, punish one man and all under Heaven submit.

literal: If only these two matters hit the mark, beauty is naturally complete.
idiomatic: If only these two are kept true, perfection follows of itself.

literal: " Shizong was greatly pleased and said: "Your words are not many, but in principle they are very important.
idiomatic: " Shizong was greatly pleased and said, "Your words are few, but in principle they matter greatly.

literal: " They clasped hands and parted.
idiomatic: " They clasped hands and parted.

literal: They defeated Xiao Ming at Hanshan; separately, with army commander Pan Yue, Bi attacked and took Liang's Tong Prefecture, and still with Yue and the others comforted the army and pitied the people — the whole circuit relied on them.
idiomatic: They defeated Xiao Ming at Hanshan; separately, with army commander Pan Yue, Bi attacked and took Liang's Tong Prefecture, and still with Yue and the others comforted the troops and showed mercy to the people — the whole circuit leaned on them.

literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month of the sixth year, the Wei emperor gathered famed monks at the Xianyang Hall to expound Buddhist doctrine; Bi, together with Minister of Personnel Yang Yin, Secretariat Director Xing Shao, Secretariat Supervisor Wei Shou, and others, all attended the dharma mat.
idiomatic: On the eighth day of the fourth month of the sixth year, the Wei emperor gathered famed monks at the Xianyang Hall to expound Buddhist doctrine; Bi, together with Minister of Personnel Yang Yin, Secretariat Director Xing Shao, Secretariat Supervisor Wei Shou, and others, all attended the dharma mat.

literal: An edict ordered Bi to ascend the lion seat and expound before the assembly.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Bi to ascend the lion seat and expound before the assembly.

literal: Zhaoxuan Director of Monks Da and the monk Daoshun, both eminent in the black-robed forest, pressed questions like blades; back and forth for several dozen rounds, none could overcome him.
idiomatic: Zhaoxuan Director of Monks Da and the monk Daoshun, both eminent in the sangha, pressed questions like blades; back and forth for several dozen rounds, none could overcome him.

literal: The emperor said: "If this worthy had been born at Confucius's gate, then what?"
idiomatic: The emperor said, "If this worthy had been born at Confucius's gate, then what?"

literal: Guanzhong sent Yitong Wang Sizheng to hold Ying Prefecture; Grand Marshal Gao Yue and others attacked him.
idiomatic: Guanzhong sent Yitong Wang Sizheng to hold Ying Prefecture; Grand Marshal Gao Yue and others attacked him.

literal: Bi handled the affairs of Ying Prefecture and acted as left director of the expeditionary secretariat.
idiomatic: Bi handled the affairs of Ying Prefecture and acted as left director of the expeditionary secretariat.

literal: At that time the great army was in the territory and levies cost much; Bi balanced suffering and joy, and both public and private interests were advanced — the people of the prefecture praised him greatly.
idiomatic: At that time the great army was in the territory and levies cost dearly; Bi balanced hardship and ease, and both public and private interests were served — the people of the prefecture praised him greatly.

literal: When Ying Prefecture was pacified, Shizong said: "Try discussing the reason Wang Sizheng was captured."
idiomatic: When Ying Prefecture was pacified, Shizong said, "Tell me why Wang Sizheng was captured."

literal: Bi said: "Sizheng did not examine the principle of rebellion and obedience, did not know the forms of great and small, and did not measure the situation of strong and weak — with these three blind spots, capture was fitting."
idiomatic: Bi said, "Sizheng did not examine the principle of rebellion and obedience, did not know the forms of great and small, and did not measure the situation of strong and weak — with these three blind spots, capture was fitting."

literal: " Shizong said: "In antiquity there was taking by rebellion and guarding by obedience; great Wu was trapped by small Yue, and weak Yan could break strong Qi.
idiomatic: " Shizong said, "In antiquity there was taking by rebellion and guarding by obedience; great Wu was trapped by small Yue, and weak Yan could break strong Qi.

literal: Your three points — how do they stand?"
idiomatic: Your three points — how do they stand?"

literal: " Bi said: "If a king is obedient but not great, great but not strong, or strong but not obedient, in principle he may be partial and would not match the sage's intent.
idiomatic: " Bi said, "If a king is obedient but not great, great but not strong, or strong but not obedient, in principle he may be partial and would not match the sage's intent.

literal: Now that all victories are combined, my crude words can stand again."
idiomatic: Now that all victories are combined, my crude words can stand again."

literal: " Shizong said: "Generally, in holding a debate one ought to have a fixed aim — how can one broadly wrap up every principle and try to secure oneself by many ends?"
idiomatic: " Shizong said, "In debate one ought to have a fixed aim — how can one wrap up every principle and try to secure oneself with many arguments?"

literal: " Bi said: "Great King's prestige and virtue combine every excellence; meaning is broad, so words are broad — it is not applying words outside the meaning."
idiomatic: " Bi said, "Great King's prestige and virtue combine every excellence; meaning is broad, so words are broad — it is not piling words beyond the meaning."

literal: " Shizong said: "If so, why was it not taken in a full year, yet when I came it fell at once?"
idiomatic: " Shizong said, "If so, why was it not taken in a full year, yet when I came it fell at once?"

literal: " Bi said: "This was surely Heaven's intent wanting to display Great King's merit."
idiomatic: " Bi said, "This was surely Heaven's intent wanting to display Great King's merit."

literal: Xianzu summoned him as concurrent chief administrator, added Guard General, transferred him to Secretariat Director, and he still served as chief administrator.
idiomatic: Xianzu summoned him as concurrent chief administrator, added guard general, transferred him to secretariat director, and he still served as chief administrator.

literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Dingyang, with a fief combined with the previous grant reaching five hundred households.
idiomatic: He was advanced in enfeoffment to marquis of Dingyang, with a fief combined with the previous grant reaching five hundred households.

literal: Bi's aim was to support and aid; there was nothing he knew of that he did not do.
idiomatic: Bi's aim was to support and aid; there was nothing he knew of that he did not do.

literal: When Xianzu was about to receive the Wei abdication, traveling from Jinyang to the capital at Pingcheng, he ordered Bi and Sikong Sima Ziru's son Ziru to ride post-horses in advance and observe the people's feelings.
idiomatic: When Xianzu was about to receive the Wei abdication, traveling from Jinyang to the capital at Pingcheng, he ordered Bi and Sikong Sima Ziru's son Ziru to ride post-horses in advance and observe the people's feelings.

literal: After he took the throne, an edict ordered the left and right document boxes brought into the Cypress Pavilion.
idiomatic: After he took the throne, an edict ordered the left and right document boxes brought into the Cypress Pavilion.

literal: For merit in deciding policy, he was promoted to Flying Cavalry General and Commandant of the Guards, and was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Chang'an.
idiomatic: For merit in deciding policy, he was promoted to flying cavalry general and commandant of the guards, and was separately enfeoffed as baron of Chang'an.

literal: Once, attending Xianzu on the Eastern Mountain together with Xing Shao, they discussed essential principles.
idiomatic: Once, attending Xianzu on the Eastern Mountain together with Xing Shao, they discussed essential principles.

literal: Xing held that when a man dies he returns to life — he feared drawing feet on a snake.
idiomatic: Xing held that when a man dies he returns to life — he feared drawing feet on a snake.

literal: Bi replied: "Generally this means that when a man dies he returns to nothing and has no power to give life.
idiomatic: Bi replied, "Generally this means that when a man dies he returns to nothing and has no power to give life.

literal: Yet things not yet born originally had no existence either; from nothing can come being — this is not regarded as doubtful. From a prior life to a later life, why alone cause wonder?"
idiomatic: Yet things not yet born originally had no existence either; from nothing can come being — this is not regarded as doubtful. From a prior life to a later life, why alone cause wonder?"

literal: " Xing said: "The sages set up teaching fundamentally to encourage and reward; therefore they use fear of what is to come so that each may attain his nature as principle hopes."
idiomatic: " Xing said, "The sages set up teaching fundamentally to encourage and reward; therefore they use fear of what is to come so that each may attain his nature as principle hopes."

literal: " Bi said: "The sages combine virtue with Heaven and Earth and equal trust to the four seasons; their speech becomes the classic and their conduct becomes law — yet you say they use emptiness to show things and deceit to encourage the people. That would be like the book in the fish's belly and unlike the edict drilled into the pillar — how could the North Star send down its light and the dragon palace hold its casket?
idiomatic: " Bi said, "The sages combine virtue with Heaven and Earth and equal trust to the four seasons; their speech becomes the classic and their conduct becomes law — yet you say they use emptiness to show things and deceit to encourage the people. That would be like the book in the fish's belly and unlike the edict drilled into the pillar — how could the North Star send down its light and the dragon palace hold its casket?

literal: Just as in your discussion, reward and fruit can melt and cast the nature of the spirit and greatly encourage moral teaching — in benefit nothing surpasses this.
idiomatic: Just as in your discussion, reward and fruit can melt and cast the nature of the spirit and greatly encourage moral teaching — in benefit nothing surpasses this.

literal: This is true teaching; why call it unreal?"
idiomatic: This is true teaching; why call it unreal?"

literal: " Xing said: "In speaking of death, 'si' means the spirit is exhausted."
idiomatic: " Xing said, "In speaking of death, 'si' means the spirit is exhausted."

literal: " Bi said: "This 'si' is like an arrow shot to exhaustion — the hand is exhausted.
idiomatic: " Bi said, "This 'si' is like an arrow shot to exhaustion — the hand is exhausted.

literal: The Xiaoya says 'no grass does not die,' and the Monthly Ordinances also says 'decaying grass dies' — plants that move and plants that stand differ, yet they belong to the same category.
idiomatic: The Xiaoya says 'no grass does not die,' and the Monthly Ordinances also says 'decaying grass dies' — plants that move and plants that stand differ, yet they belong to the same category.

literal: Unfeeling plants can still return to life; things that hold spirit — why should re-creation be hindered?
idiomatic: Unfeeling plants can still return to life; things that hold spirit — why should re-creation be hindered?

literal: If you say that when grass dies seed still remains within, then again when a man dies there is also consciousness.
idiomatic: If you say that when grass dies seed still remains within, then again when a man dies there is also consciousness.

literal: Seed and consciousness are not seen and are therefore called nonexistent.
idiomatic: Seed and consciousness are not seen and are therefore called nonexistent.

literal: Spirit in the form is also not self-visible; even Li Zhu's brightness cannot see it.
idiomatic: Spirit in the form is also not self-visible; even Li Zhu's brightness cannot see it.

literal: Though Mencius could examine the pupils, worthy and foolish could be distinguished;
idiomatic: Though Mencius could examine the pupils, worthy and foolish could be distinguished;

literal: Zhong You, hearing music, made mountains and waters appear in form —
idiomatic: Zhong You, hearing music, made mountains and waters appear in form —

literal: yet these are the spirit's workmanship; how are they the spirit's substance?
idiomatic: yet these are the spirit's workmanship; how are they the spirit's substance?

literal: It is like jade and silk not being ritual, or bells and drums not being music; push from this and the meaning is seen."
idiomatic: It is like jade and silk not being ritual, or bells and drums not being music; push from this and the meaning is seen."

literal: " Xing said: "When Ji Zha said 'nothing does not go,' he also meant scattered exhaustion; if it gathers again to become a thing, one cannot say 'nothing does not go.'"
idiomatic: " Xing said, "When Ji Zha said 'nothing does not go,' he also meant scattered exhaustion; if it gathers again to become a thing, one cannot say 'nothing does not go.'"

literal: " Bi said: "Flesh and bone below return to earth, while soul and breath then have nowhere they do not go — this is the form fallen and the soul roaming; gone, yet not exhausted.
idiomatic: " Bi said, "Flesh and bone below return to earth, while soul and breath then have nowhere they do not go — this is the form fallen and the soul roaming; gone, yet not exhausted.

literal: It is like a bird leaving the nest or a snake leaving its hole.
idiomatic: It is like a bird leaving the nest or a snake leaving its hole.

literal: Because something still exists, there is nowhere it does not go; if you make it nothing, where would it go?
idiomatic: Because something still exists, there is nowhere it does not go; if you make it nothing, where would it go?

literal: Yanling had the knowledge to discern the subtle and knew that it does not follow the form;
idiomatic: Yanling had the knowledge to discern the subtle and knew that it does not follow the form;

literal: Confucius uttered a sigh at studying the rites and praised that it differs from the form.
idiomatic: Confucius uttered a sigh at studying the rites and praised that it differs from the form.

literal: If you permit the broad and empty, then everyone would be Ji Zi.
idiomatic: If you permit the broad and empty, then everyone would be Ji Zi.

literal: This is not called lofty discourse — to hold this as nothing."
idiomatic: This is not called lofty discourse — to hold this as nothing."

literal: " Xing said: "Spirit in a person is like light in a candle; when the candle is exhausted the light ends, and when the person dies the spirit perishes."
idiomatic: " Xing said, "Spirit in a person is like light in a candle; when the candle is exhausted the light ends, and when the person dies the spirit perishes."

literal: " Bi said: "The old learning and former Confucians have this saying every time; the crowd's doubts and the multitude's confusions all arise from this.
idiomatic: " Bi said, "The old learning and former Confucians repeat this saying; the crowd's doubts and the multitude's confusions all arise from this.

literal: Generally, those who discriminate are not refined and those who think are not earnest.
idiomatic: Generally, those who discriminate are not refined and those who think are not earnest.

literal: I have a slight point not yet seen that can be verified thereby.
idiomatic: I have a slight point not yet seen that can be verified thereby.

literal: A candle generates light because of its substance; the larger the substance, the larger the light.
idiomatic: A candle generates light because of its substance; the larger the substance, the larger the light.

literal: A person is not one whose spirit is tied to the form; the smaller the form, the spirit is not smaller.
idiomatic: A person is not one whose spirit is tied to the form; the smaller the form, the spirit is not smaller.

literal: Thus Confucius's wisdom was certainly not shorter than the Long Di's;
idiomatic: Thus Confucius's wisdom was certainly not shorter than the Long Di's;

literal: Cao Cao's heroism was far beyond Cui Yan's.
idiomatic: Cao Cao's heroism was far beyond Cui Yan's.

literal: Spirit to form is also like a lord having a state.
idiomatic: Spirit to form is also like a lord having a state.

literal: The state is truly what the lord governs; the lord is not what the state gives birth to.
idiomatic: The state is truly what the lord governs; the lord is not what the state gives birth to.

literal: Not born together — who says they perish together?"
idiomatic: Not born together — who says they perish together?"

literal: " Xing said: "Leaving this and adapting to that — birth upon birth is always present.
idiomatic: " Xing said, "Leaving this and adapting to that — birth upon birth is always present.

literal: Should Zhou and Confucius not be the same as Zhuang Zhou drumming on a pot and harmonizing with Sanghu's following song?"
idiomatic: Should Zhou and Confucius not be the same as Zhuang Zhou drumming on a pot and harmonizing with Sanghu's following song?"

literal: " Bi said: "Sharing shade and resting still has the sorrow of impending parting;
idiomatic: " Bi said, "Sharing shade and resting still has the sorrow of impending parting;

literal: driving an exhausted cart to roam also has the sigh of mid-journey.
idiomatic: driving an exhausted cart to roam also has the sigh of mid-journey.

literal: How much more when bodies joined and breath shared are transformed into different things — mourning suited to feeling; what harm to a sage?"
idiomatic: How much more when bodies joined and breath shared are transformed into different things — mourning suited to feeling; what harm to a sage?"

literal: " Xing said: "A hawk transforms into a dove, a rat changes into a quail, and a yellow mother into a turtle — all are categories of birth.
idiomatic: " Xing said, "A hawk transforms into a dove, a rat changes into a quail, and a yellow mother into a turtle — all are categories of birth.

literal: Categories transform yet give birth to one another, like light leaving this candle and again igniting that candle."
idiomatic: Categories transform yet give birth to one another, like light leaving this candle and again igniting that candle."

literal: " Bi said: "Before the hawk has transformed into a dove, the dove does not exist.
idiomatic: " Bi said, "Before the hawk has transformed into a dove, the dove does not exist.

literal: If the rat already has two existences, how can both stand?
idiomatic: If the rat already has two existences, how can both stand?

literal: Light leaves this candle and can ignite that candle; spirit leaves this form and also entrusts itself to that form — again, what confusion?"
idiomatic: Light leaves this candle and can ignite that candle; spirit leaves this form and also entrusts itself to that form — again, what confusion?"

literal: " Xing said: "To want earth to transform into a human and wood to grow eyes and a nose — creation's spirit ought not to be like this."
idiomatic: " Xing said, "To want earth to transform into a human and wood to grow eyes and a nose — creation's spirit ought not to be like this."

literal: " Bi said: "Rotten grass becomes fireflies and old wood scorpions — creation cannot do it; who makes it so of itself?"
idiomatic: " Bi said, "Rotten grass becomes fireflies and old wood scorpions — creation cannot do it; who makes it so of itself?"

literal: Afterward he separately wrote Xing a letter saying: "In establishing words and clarifying principle, one ought to issue from canonical evidence; yet you turn your back on Confucius and Buddha and stand alone as a gentleman.
idiomatic: Afterward he separately wrote Xing a letter saying, "In establishing words and clarifying principle, one ought to issue from canonical evidence; yet you turn your back on Confucius and Buddha and stand alone as a gentleman.

literal: If one does not take the sages as teachers, each thing has its own heart — if the horse's head wants east, who can resist?
idiomatic: If one does not take the sages as teachers, each thing has its own heart — if the horse's head wants east, who can resist?

literal: What is taken from hitting the center, and what is valued in obtaining the one?
idiomatic: What is taken from hitting the center, and what is valued in obtaining the one?

literal: Elegant rhyme though high, narrow view not understood."
idiomatic: Elegant rhyme though high, narrow view not understood."

literal: " Before and after, back and forth again and again three times; Xing Shao's principle was bent and he stopped — much of the text is not recorded.
idiomatic: " Before and after, back and forth again and again three times; Xing Shao's argument gave way and he stopped — much of the text is not recorded.
